question: What protection prevents poison from entering the body even when one has been bitten by great serpents?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison would normally be expected to enter the body.
Under the stated condition, poison does not enter the body.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
uncertainties: The source of this protection is presupposed from the preceding practice.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
